purpose: Teach: 見送る/盗む/つど/痛快/くどい/本末転倒/滴/モニカ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんを、絶対、見送る、絶対、駅、絶対、寂しかったわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, you remember — when you were young, seeing off the grandkids at the station… it was lonely, wasn't it?
lines.style: Soft, reaching back into old memory. Measured pace, slight upward questioning lilt at the end. Genuine curiosity beneath the wistfulness. Not performing nostalgia — inhabiting it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、お祖父ちゃんから、絶対、お料理のコツ、絶対、盗む、絶対、ように、絶対、覚えたわよ、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When I was young, I used to watch your father so carefully in the kitchen — picked up all his little tricks, you know. I remember.
lines.style: Warm, immediate recognition. Soft smile in the voice. Speaking as though she can still see those moments. Gentle pace, comfortable pauses. The ease of someone recalling something beloved.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、お客様の前を通る、絶対、つど、絶対、丁寧に、絶対、ご挨拶、絶対、したぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, your father — every single customer who passed by the shop, he'd bow and greet them so politely. Do you remember, Gran?
lines.style: Quiet pride underneath. Slight warmth on the memory of his courtesy. Even pace. Gentle check at the end — asking her to confirm he saw it right. Not boasting, just remembering together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、痛快、絶対、な、絶対、笑い話、絶対、ばあさんに、絶対、よく、絶対、聞かせてくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes, and your grandfather used to tell me the most wonderful, funny stories. He'd come home with something that made me laugh every time.
lines.style: Bright recall, genuine laughter in the memory. Slightly faster pace — stories naturally move quicker. Voice opens up a little. The unmistakable warmth of a woman who heard those stories and loved the man telling them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さんの、絶対、お話、絶対、くどい、絶対、と、絶対、ばあさんに、絶対、笑われたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your father's stories, though — they did go on a bit. I used to tease him about it, remember?
lines.style: Gentle, affectionate teasing in the voice. Not mean, but honest. A slight twinkle — the kind of thing you'd say about someone you loved. Quick, light delivery. Expecting her to join in.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、本末転倒、絶対、にならぬよう、絶対、優先順位、絶対、つけていたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Your grandfather was always so careful about what mattered most. He never let things get backwards — he knew what came first.
lines.style: Admiring, steady. A note of quiet respect. She's describing someone she learned from. Measured pace, each phrase weighted. Gentle but clear — this was something she valued and watched him do.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、軒先の、絶対、雨の、絶対、滴、絶対、お父さん、絶対、よく、絶対、眺めたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, your father would stand at the eaves on a rainy day and just… watch the raindrops fall. He'd stand there for the longest time.
lines.style: Soft, almost dreamlike. Slow pace. Each image lands gently. A slight breathiness — remembering something both small and somehow significant. Trailing off slightly, as though he's still there, still watching.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ご近所の、絶対、モニカ、絶対、さん、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、よく、絶対、お話したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Our neighbor Monica — do you remember her? She and your grandfather used to talk for hours. Such good conversations they had.
lines.style: Warm, conversational. A gentle smile. The tone of someone bringing up an old friend fondly. Measured, unhurried — she's not rushing through it. Small warmth on 'Monica' and 'your grandfather' — people who mattered.
